Messages.Author: Jozxyqk
Messages.Body:
So let's say an Archbishop gets a Writ of Acceptance.
He then "gives up" his title until he becomes Sabbat
again.

But, while he is Camarilla, suppose he calls a Praxis
Seizure, and becomes a Prince.
Then he drops his Writ.

Is he title-less as Sabbat, or does he get his Archbishop
title back since he isn't a Prince?
Will he gain his Prince title back if he changes back to
Camarilla?

Basically, does the "one title at a time" rule apply if the title is
"inactive" at the time?

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
>So let's say an Archbishop gets a Writ of Acceptance.
>He then "gives up" his title until he becomes Sabbat
>again.
>
>But, while he is Camarilla, suppose he calls a Praxis
>Seizure, and becomes a Prince.
>Then he drops his Writ.

As soon as he becomes a Prince, he yields his old title. See (from Section 10
of the Rulebook):

A vampire must belong to the appropriate sect to receive a title. If a vampire
with a title changes clans or sects to a clan or sect inappropriate for his
title, he loses the benefit of the title until his clan or sect changes
appropriately. If he receives a new title, or if his title is contested (see
Contested Titles, sec. 4.2), he immediately yields the old title.

>Is he title-less as Sabbat, or does he get his Archbishop
>title back since he isn't a Prince?

He is title-less Sabbat.

>Will he gain his Prince title back if he changes back to
>Camarilla?

Assuming that he hasn't gained another title and his title hasn't been
contested in the mean time, then yes be regains his Princeliness.

>Basically, does the "one title at a time" rule apply if the title is
>"inactive" at the time?

Yes. Once again see Section 10 of the on-line rulebook.

Halcyan 2
